description:
Use this when the user wants to create, inspect or change anything in their open Adobe InDesign documents (Sidekick for InDesign).

Execute JavaScript code in InDesign via UXP (NOT ExtendScript). The code has access to the full InDesign DOM via require('indesign'). The 'app' object is NOT a global — you must import it: const { app } = require('indesign'). Use 'return' to return values.

Capabilities:
- Full InDesign DOM access (documents, pages, text frames, styles, etc.)
- Async/await supported - Promises are awaited before returning
- File operations via UXP storage APIs (with sandbox restrictions)

Units (IMPORTANT):
- Always specify units explicitly as strings: "12pt", "1in", "5mm", "6p" (picas)
- Bare numbers use the document's current measurement units - this causes unpredictable results
- Examples: fontSize = "11pt", leading = "14pt", margins = "0.5in", textFrameHeight = "200pt"
- WRONG: fontSize = 11 (will be interpreted as 11 of whatever unit the doc uses)

Limitations:
- File system is sandboxed - cannot freely access arbitrary paths; doc.fullName returns a Promise that may fail
- No shell command execution (no app.system())
- No inter-app communication (no BridgeTalk)
- Return values must be JSON-serializable
- Text encoding limited to UTF-8

InDesign DOM quirks:
- Many properties are type-dependent; accessing a property that doesn't apply throws "The property is not applicable in the current state" - always check object type first or use try/catch
- Text variables have different variableOptions depending on variableType (e.g., CUSTOM_TEXT_TYPE has contents, others don't)
- COLLECTION INDEXING: Bracket notation does NOT work in UXP (doc.pages[0] returns undefined). Use these instead:
  - doc.pages.item(0) - for single item by index
  - doc.pages.firstItem() / doc.pages.lastItem() - for first/last
  - doc.pages.everyItem().getElements() - to get a real JS array for forEach/map/filter
- OBJECT COMPARISON: UXP DOM objects and enums don't support === or ==. Use the .equals() method:
  - WRONG: page.side === PageSideOptions.RIGHT_HAND (always false)
  - WRONG: frame1 === frame2 (always false, even for same object)
  - RIGHT: page.side.equals(PageSideOptions.RIGHT_HAND)
  - RIGHT: frame1.equals(frame2)
- ENUM VALUES (IMPORTANT): Always use enum objects, NEVER integer codes.
  - WRONG: frame.textFramePreferences.autoSizingType = 1634494067 (hallucinated number)
  - WRONG: doc.exportFile(1952403524, filePath)
  - RIGHT: Import and use enum objects:
      const { AutoSizingTypeEnum, ExportFormat } = require('indesign');
      frame.textFramePreferences.autoSizingType = AutoSizingTypeEnum.HEIGHT_AND_WIDTH;
      doc.exportFile(ExportFormat.PDF_TYPE, filePath);
  - Common enums: AutoSizingTypeEnum, VerticalJustification, PageSideOptions, ScriptLanguage, ExportFormat, FitOptions
  - Always import enums from 'indesign' before use
- PARAGRAPH BREAKS: Use \r (carriage return) for paragraph breaks, NOT \n (newline). Using \n causes text to render without word spacing.
  - WRONG: "First paragraph.\nSecond paragraph."
  - RIGHT: "First paragraph.\rSecond paragraph."
- STYLE OVERRIDES: Use para.clearOverrides(OverrideType.ALL) to clear all overrides. Import OverrideType from 'indesign'. Best practice: create and apply paragraph styles rather than direct formatting.
- TRACKING HIGHLIGHT: Non-zero tracking in paragraph styles triggers InDesign's Style Override Highlighter (light blue background). This is normal InDesign behavior, not a bug. It's UI-only - doesn't affect output. Toggle off with [a+] button in Paragraph Styles panel.
- Some properties that were synchronous in ExtendScript return Promises in UXP (e.g., doc.fullName)
- Master spread pages may not be accessible immediately after document creation; doc.masterSpreads[0].pages can be undefined. Instead of iterating master spread pages to set margins, pass marginPreferences directly to documents.add()

Facing pages & margins:
- When facingPages=true, set margins as inside (gutter) and outside values using left and right properties
- Use the SAME margin values on ALL pages - InDesign automatically mirrors them visually
- marginPreferences.left = inside/gutter margin (smaller), marginPreferences.right = outside margin (larger)
- Margin data will appear identical for all pages when queried - this is correct; InDesign handles visual mirroring internally

Text frames on facing pages (IMPORTANT - different from margins!):
- geometricBounds are NOT automatically mirrored - you must calculate different coordinates for recto vs verso pages
- Use page.side to detect: PageSideOptions.RIGHT_HAND = recto, PageSideOptions.LEFT_HAND = verso
- Use page.marginPreferences (not doc.marginPreferences) for accurate margin values
- Recto (right page): left edge uses inner margin (mb.left), right edge uses outer (mb.right)
- Verso (left page): left edge uses outer margin (mb.right), right edge uses inner (mb.left)

BEFORE PLACING TEXT FRAMES:
Use the get_layout tool to get page dimensions and pre-calculated contentArea coordinates. The contentArea bounds can be used directly for geometricBounds - use the raw numeric values without adding unit suffixes.

geometricBounds format is [top, left, bottom, right]. The get_layout tool returns values in the document's measurement units (check the measurementUnits field). Use these values directly as numbers.

OBJECT NAMING (IMPORTANT):
- Always set both 'name' and 'label' properties on created objects (text frames, graphic frames, rectangles, groups, etc.)
- name: Human-readable for Layers panel (e.g., "Header Text Frame", "Main Body", "Logo Image")
- label: Script-friendly with sidekick_ prefix, lowercase with underscores (e.g., "sidekick_header_text_frame", "sidekick_main_body")
- Example:
    const frame = page.textFrames.add();
    frame.name = "Header Text Frame";
    frame.label = "sidekick_header_text_frame";
- This enables users to find Sidekick-created objects in the Layers panel and via scripts

actions.description: Saved actions to call from the code, by name (list_actions lists them). Each becomes an async function named in camelCase -- alt-text-audit becomes altTextAudit -- taking the action's params as one object, with the header's defaults filled in, and returning exactly what the action's main returned (usually a report object { summary, items, changeCount, data }; a bare string is possible -- check before reading .items): const audit = await altTextAudit({ scope: 'document' }); audit.items.length. Use this rather than pasting an action's source into the code.

code.description: JavaScript code to execute in InDesign

description.description:
Brief description shown in the InDesign plugin panel. REQUIRED FORMAT:

Line 1: What Sidekick is doing (present progressive tense, e.g., 'Getting the page count')

Line 2: Manual alternative with keyboard shortcut if applicable (e.g., 'You can also use **File > Document Setup** (`Cmd+Option+P`)')

ALWAYS include the manual alternative on line 2 when there's a simple UI equivalent. Only omit for complex scripting tasks with no UI equivalent. Supports markdown: **bold**, `code`.
